evidence.title: Khowai
evidence.text: Khowai is a town located in the Indian state of Tripura and a recent nagar panchayat forming into a Khowai Municipal Council in newly formed Khowai district in the Indian state of Tripura.

evidence.title: Khowai
evidence.text: The city lies on the banks of Khowai river and hence from the river the city gets its name.

evidence.title: Khowai
evidence.text: Located near the bangladesh border it has boundaries with it on its entire Southern part.

evidence.title: Qayyarah
evidence.text: Qayyarah or Qayara (Arabic: القيارة‎ ‎ ) is an Iraqi town located in southern Nineveh Governorate on the west bank of the Tigris river, and about 60 km (35 miles) south of Mosul.

evidence.title: Qayyarah
evidence.text: It is located in the Mosul District, and it is the seat of Qayyarah subdistrict.

evidence.title: Qayyarah
evidence.text: It has a population of 15,000.

evidence.title: Qayyarah
evidence.text: The town is located near the Qayyarah oil field and has an oil refinery on its south-western outskirts.

evidence.title: Qayyarah
evidence.text: The Qayyarah Airfield West is 20 kilometers west of the town.

evidence.title: Menindee, New South Wales
evidence.text: Menindee, frequently but erroneously spelled "Menindie", is a small town in the far west of New South Wales, Australia, in Central Darling Shire, on the banks of the Darling River, with a sign-posted population of 980 and a 2011 census population of 449.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: Boundary is a ghost town located in Stevens County, Washington, United States.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: The town was located near the Canada–US border and near the Columbia River.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: Boundary's peak years were during the 1890s.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: The population was around 900.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: The town started off as a railroad camp.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: When the railroad finally spanned the wild Pend Oreille with a bridge, the railroad workers quickly moved on leaving the town of Boundary deserted.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: The town contained the Boundary Hotel, post office, and general store.

evidence.title: Boundary, Washington
evidence.text: A town called "New Boundary" came into being south of the original townsite and the old town eventually vanished.

evidence.title: Menindee County
evidence.text: Menindee County is one of the 141 Cadastral divisions of New South Wales.

evidence.title: Menindee County
evidence.text: It is located between the Darling River and the South Australian border.

evidence.title: Menindee County
evidence.text: Menindee is at its north-eastern edge.

evidence.title: Menindee County
evidence.text: The Menindee Lakes are located there.

evidence.title: Menindee Lakes
evidence.text: The Menindee Lakes is a chain of shallow ephemeral freshwater lakes connected to the Darling River to form a storage system.

evidence.title: Menindee Lakes
evidence.text: The lakes lie in the far west region of New South Wales, Australia, near the town of Menindee.

evidence.title: Gregory, Queensland
evidence.text: Gregory is a small town located near the Gregory River in the Shire of Burke, Queensland, Australia.

evidence.title: Gregory, Queensland
evidence.text: The town had a population of 40 people in 2008 and is situated on the banks of the perennial Gregory River.

evidence.title: Gregory, Queensland
evidence.text: The Gregory River was named by explorer William Landsborough on 19 November 1861, after Augustus Charles Gregory explorer and first Surveyor General of Queensland.

evidence.title: Volcanic City
evidence.text: Volcanic City is a ghost town located in the Boundary Country region of British Columbia.

evidence.title: Volcanic City
evidence.text: It is located near the north fork of the Kettle River.

evidence.title: Volcanic City
evidence.text: A prospector named Volcanic Brown discovered an "iron cap" mountain near the north fork of the Kettle river.

evidence.title: Volcanic City
evidence.text: Volcanic Brown claimed the mountain was rich for mining.

evidence.title: Volcanic City
evidence.text: Brown tried to create a city in the vicinity of the mountain.

evidence.title: Volcanic City
evidence.text: He assumed miners would be attracted to the mountain and they would live in the city.

evidence.title: Bridal Veil, Oregon
evidence.text: Bridal Veil is a virtual ghost town located in Multnomah County, Oregon, United States.

evidence.title: Bridal Veil, Oregon
evidence.text: It was established in the 1880s during a logging boom by a logging company as it harvested timber on nearby Larch Mountain to be a company mill town around a sawmill.

evidence.title: Bridal Veil, Oregon
evidence.text: It had a close relationship with the logging town of Palmer for the first 50 years of its history.

evidence.title: Bridal Veil, Oregon
evidence.text: As of November 2011, all that remains of the town is a post office and a cemetery.

evidence.title: Bridal Veil, Oregon
evidence.text: The site is located near the west end of the Columbia River Gorge.

evidence.title: Binnaway, New South Wales
evidence.text: Binnaway is a small town located on the Castlereagh River in central western New South Wales near the larger centre of Coonabarabran, which is about 35 kilometres to the north.

evidence.title: Binnaway, New South Wales
evidence.text: In 2006, the town had a population of 495 people.

evidence.title: Binnaway, New South Wales
evidence.text: The road linking these two towns closely follows the meandering Castlereagh River.

evidence.title: Binnaway, New South Wales
evidence.text: There are many pleasant areas to stop beside the road and on the river banks to have a picnic.

evidence.title: Binnaway, New South Wales
evidence.text: Binnaway is also located near the similarly sized small town of Mendooran.

evidence.title: Binnaway, New South Wales
evidence.text: Following local government amalgamation, the town is now located in the Warrumbungle Shire Council area which is headquartered at Coonabarabran.
